## Wave 22 compact integration and acceptance packet — Exploration Cartography And Archive

The wave remains a documentation-only proposal over **survey signal and commons**. Before implementation, verify owner, consumer, route, save, replay, accessibility, performance, and rollback. The high-volume bank must pass a representative sample before expansion. Story branches must change a reachable owner state or projection and retain a coherent refusal path. Any missing seam, duplicate authority, unowned mechanic, or contradictory save contract stops the packet and returns it to premise review.

**Five-point handoff:** (1) current-source premise and collision search; (2) one owner and one event/save seam; (3) data, localization, migration, and validator evidence; (4) player route, side-quest callback, replay, accessibility, and performance evidence; (5) exact files, focused verification, limitations, rollback, and next audit.

## Continuation Wave 23 — Plan 8 — Exploration Cartography And Archive

Wave 23 adds a fresh, owner-bound expansion layer for **exploration cartography and archive**. It is a planning scaffold only. The current 30-field structure remains active; these passes add new playable seams, high-volume authoring, story callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **cartography, expedition, installation, fragment, codex, journal, and archive owners**. Material anchors include **a map mark crossed in blue, an instrument wrapped in canvas, a label carrying two dates, and a blank margin left open**. Observable markers include **coordinate confidence, instrument condition, provenance age, access condition, route freshness, and archive status**.

### Pass 232 — Survey Confidence Records

This pass tests how **survey confidence records** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over cartography, expedition, installation, fragment, codex, journal, and archive owners; it does not add a second exploration cartography and archive authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Survey Confidence Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees coordinate confidence, instrument condition, provenance age, access condition, route freshness, and archive status with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Survey Confidence Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Survey Confidence Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Survey Confidence Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present coordinate confidence, instrument condition, provenance age, access condition, route freshness, and archive status as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Survey Confidence Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross coordinate confidence, instrument condition, provenance age, access condition, route freshness, and archive status with the material anchors a map mark crossed in blue, an instrument wrapped in canvas, a label carrying two dates, and a blank margin left open. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Survey Confidence Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Survey Confidence Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Survey Confidence Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Survey Confidence Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Survey Confidence Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 23 high-volume content and story bank — Exploration Cartography And Archive

This bank expands **exploration cartography and archive** through the existing **cartography, expedition, installation, fragment, codex, journal, and archive owners**. It is authored content and verification scaffolding, not a second authority. Every row carries a stable snake_case ID, schema version, source reference, lifecycle status, localization key, owner, and rollback note. The bank is exercised against **coordinate confidence, instrument condition, provenance age, access condition, route freshness, and archive status** and uses **a map mark crossed in blue, an instrument wrapped in canvas, a label carrying two dates, and a blank margin left open** as material evidence.

### High-volume field 1 — Witness proof families

The **witness proof families** field covers **witness, confidence, sample, hold, evidence, release, and refusal**. Start with a representative sample, validate it through the current loader and catalog integrity path, then expand by bounded pages. Reject duplicate IDs, unresolved references, unsupported effects, contradictory lifecycle values, and rows with no reachable consumer. Each row states whether it is authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state; a mutable result stays with its canonical owner.

For play, begin with an observable disturbance and offer verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved results. At least one row crosses three existing domains and changes a visible route, relationship boundary, room condition, map confidence, archive entry, or expedition timing. The callback names its publisher, consumer, consequence owner, and source age.

The host supports pagination, filtering, loading, empty, stale, redacted, and error states. Long localization wraps, focus survives refresh, and uncertainty is written rather than encoded by color. Measure first-page latency, allocations, event fan-out, save delta, and safe degradation. A deterministic fixture repeats the same seed and ordered inputs after save and reload. The receipt records source paths, owner evidence, unresolved collisions, migration behavior, rollback, and the stop line if the premise fails.

**Field receipt:** sample IDs; owner API; source references; state ladder; side-quest hook; localization keys; pagination budget; replay fixture; rollback path.

## Continuation Wave 24 — Plan 8 — Exploration Cartography And Archive

Wave 24 adds a fresh, owner-bound expansion layer for **exploration cartography and archive**. It is a planning scaffold only. The current 30-field structure remains active; these passes add new playable seams, high-volume authoring, story callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **cartography, expedition, installation, fragment, codex, journal, and archive owners**. Material anchors include **a compass with a missing screw, a charcoal line over old ink, a specimen tag with a blank field, and a folded map corner**. Observable markers include **bearing confidence, instrument readiness, provenance gap, access window, route revision, and archive custody**.

### Pass 243 — Survey Confidence Cards

This pass tests how **survey confidence cards** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over cartography, expedition, installation, fragment, codex, journal, and archive owners; it does not add a second exploration cartography and archive authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Survey Confidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees bearing confidence, instrument readiness, provenance gap, access window, route revision, and archive custody with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Survey Confidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Survey Confidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Survey Confidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present bearing confidence, instrument readiness, provenance gap, access window, route revision, and archive custody as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Survey Confidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross bearing confidence, instrument readiness, provenance gap, access window, route revision, and archive custody with the material anchors a compass with a missing screw, a charcoal line over old ink, a specimen tag with a blank field, and a folded map corner. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Survey Confidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Survey Confidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Survey Confidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Survey Confidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Survey Confidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 24 compact integration and acceptance packet — Exploration Cartography And Archive

The wave remains a documentation-only proposal over **bearing revisions and archive custody**. Before implementation, verify owner, consumer, route, save, replay, accessibility, performance, and rollback. The high-volume bank must pass a representative sample before expansion. Story branches must change a reachable owner state or projection and retain a coherent refusal path. Any missing seam, duplicate authority, unowned mechanic, or contradictory save contract stops the packet and returns it to premise review.

**Five-point handoff:** (1) current-source premise and collision search; (2) one owner and one event/save seam; (3) data, localization, migration, and validator evidence; (4) player route, side-quest callback, replay, accessibility, and performance evidence; (5) exact files, focused verification, limitations, rollback, and next audit.

## Plans 5–8 closeout — Plan 8 integration packet

**Closeout state:** planning-complete, implementation-unclaimed. Plan 8 is ready for a premise audit of one provenance-aware survey projection over the current cartography, expedition, installation, fragment, codex, journal, or archive owner. The first slice reads an observation, displays coordinate confidence, instrument condition, provenance age, and custody, and routes verify, annotate, defer, or return through the owner. It does not add a second map, fragment inventory, archive, or expedition scheduler.

**Required evidence before implementation:** current observation producer and revision API; one reachable archive or map consumer; one schema-valid survey row; idempotent correction behavior; save/stateless proof; deterministic ordered observations; pagination and focus behavior; uncertainty text and sound-off path; one return callback; rollback adapter. Stop if an observation cannot be traced to a producer, if a citation mutates archive state directly, or if a map projection stores a second coordinate truth.

**Integration order:** expedition/installation observation → cartography owner → fragment/codex/archive projection → journal or narrative callback → UI refresh. Downstream readers preserve provenance and uncertainty and ignore duplicate revisions. The handoff must list unresolved landmark IDs and distinguish authored clues from verified coordinates.


## Wave 35 integration closeout receipt — Plan 8: Exploration Cartography and Archive

**Closeout status:** documentation-only; READY FOR PREMISE AUDIT. This receipt does not claim implementation.

**Program role:** cartography, expedition, installation, fragment, codex, journal, archive, and provenance

**Primary owners:** cartography, expedition, installation, fragment, codex, journal, archive, and provenance owners

**Required delta:** a provenance-aware survey projection over one existing observation, with deterministic revision, uncertainty, and archive custody

**First safe slice:** one survey mark corrected after a return trip and cited in an existing archive surface

**Evidence anchors:** a survey pin, a weathered compass card, a fragment sleeve, and a map margin note

**Observable signals:** coordinate confidence, instrument condition, provenance age, archive custody, route risk, and correction state

### Closeout boundary

The plan closes at the design boundary where one current owner can publish a fact, one consumer can display or consume it, one command can be issued through the owner, and one recovery path can return the player to a known state. The plan does not create a second ledger, registry, cache authority, save store, event bus, or presentation-owned counter. A row remains design-only until a current source search proves its consumer.

### Integration contract

The first receipt must identify the owner, public API, data file, save section or stateless proof, host route, focused tests, and rollback. It must exercise source age, stale input, duplicate delivery, interruption, correction, keyboard/controller parity, empty and error states, and one delayed content callback. The same seed and ordered inputs must reproduce the result across save, reload, host reopen, and duplicate event delivery.

### Content and failure gate

The first content slice uses survey crews, corrected maps, lost instruments, archive disputes, return trips, and evidence callbacks. It includes discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, choice, quiet success, costly success, refusal, unresolved outcome, delayed callback, repeat policy, and retirement rule. It must stop safely for second map, fragment inventory duplication, non-deterministic ordering, false certainty, and archive overwrite. Prose can describe evidence and uncertainty but cannot create a gameplay fact.

### Handoff

**MUST PRESERVE:** existing authority, engine-free Core, JSON data authority, deterministic ordering, current save ownership, truthful UI, and active path claims.

**MUST ADD:** one premise receipt, one owner-bound slice, one validator-backed sample, one replay or stateless proof, one accessible route, one focused verification result, and one rollback note.

**MUST NOT DO:** duplicate state, revive retired architecture, claim runtime integration from document volume, or widen the catalog before reachability.

**NEXT ACTION:** run the bounded premise audit for the first safe slice and return the evidence to the integrator.
